extracted.intended_audience: QHP issuers, FFE State officials performing plan management, Exchange regulators, and other stakeholders commenting on non-network plan certification
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed criteria and review factors for certifying non-network Qualified Health Plans (QHPs) offered through Federally-facilitated Exchanges (FFEs) and for determining whether an FFE State has authority and technical capacity to conduct provider and ECP certification reviews of non-network plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous outreach to providers
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-network plan must have in place a strategy for conducting continuous outreach to available providers (including ECPs) in a particular area to determine whether they would accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers not under contract may change charges at any time; continuous outreach lets the plan determine acceptance and adjust benefit amounts so enrollees can access a sufficient number of providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of benefit amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-network plan's strategy for making benefit amounts available to the public, including plan enrollees, potential enrollees, and providers (including ECPs), in an easily accessible and understandable format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making this information widely available would give notice to providers charging more than the plan's benefit amount and enable enrollees to understand what the plan will pay so they can shop for care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for determining benefit amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-network plan's methodology for determining benefit amounts, demonstrating that benefit amounts are not arbitrary but are informed through analyses and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an important indicator that benefit amounts reasonably cover costs associated with particular services; HHS expects well-documented analyses supporting amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer information on balance billing and expected OOP costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan's strategy for providing consumer-friendly information to enrollees and potential enrollees about potential balance billing scenarios and expected out-of-pocket (OOP) costs, including historical data on actual OOP costs incurred by enrollees while accessing ECPs in the area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because non-network plans may be unfamiliar to enrollees, plans must educate enrollees on how to use the plan to minimize additional OOP costs; historical OOP data helps set realistic expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of exceptions process
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of an exceptions process under the non-network plan for enrollees who cannot find providers (including ECPs) willing to accept the benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exceptions process recognizes circumstances where many providers refuse the plan's payment; it could shift the burden of unavoidable additional OOP costs from the enrollee to the non-network plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer service and provider directory assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-network plan's strategy for providing adequate customer service or online provider directory assistance resources to help enrollees and potential enrollees find providers (including ECPs) in their area who will accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customer assistance is an important indicator of the plan's ability to educate enrollees and minimize OOP costs by helping them find accepting providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with general QHP certification criteria (§155.1000(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans must be subject to and demonstrate they meet all general QHP certification criteria at §155.1000(c), including minimum certification requirements in subpart C of part 156.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes providing the EHB package (§156.20), EHB in accordance with §156.115, cost-sharing at §156.130, and levels of coverage at §156.140; failure to comply may result in denial or decertification (§155.1000(e), §155.1080(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of Essential Health Benefits (EHB) comparable to State benchmark
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that non-network plans provide benefits substantially equal to the relevant State's EHB-benchmark plan and not treat state non-EHB benefits as EHB under the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the requirement to provide EHB in accordance with §156.115 and is a condition of QHP certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer protections applicable to individual and small group coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans applying for QHP certification must be structured to provide all consumer protections that apply to individual and small group health coverage (including PHS Act title XXVII parts A–D); they may not claim exemption solely because they do not contract with providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to offer these protections can result in denial or decertification under §155.1000(e) and §155.1080(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange authority to deny certification under 'in the interest' standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 1311(e)(1)(B) and §155.1000(c)(2), Exchanges may determine whether a plan is in the interest of qualified individuals and employers and may deny certification even if minimum requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges may use strategies such as 'any qualified plan', competitive selection, negotiation with issuers, or implement selection criteria beyond minimum standards to protect enrollees' interests (e.g., protection against surprise medical bills).

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for HHS-RADV and medical record access
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that non-network plans may have difficulty obtaining medical records from providers for HHS-RADV, potentially resulting in non-validated diagnoses and higher error rates in risk adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS seeks comment on considerations for non-network plans in HHS-RADV processes given EDGE-reported diagnoses without medical records are unvalidated and affect adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE State Effective Provider Access Review Program criteria (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: An FFE State electing to conduct provider access certification reviews must demonstrate sufficient authority and technical capacity by satisfying applicable criteria to be considered to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program under proposed §155.1050(d)(2)-(d)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State elects not to or does not satisfy criteria, HHS would conduct provider access reviews under §156.230 for network plans and under proposed §156.236 for non-network plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider access parity for non-network plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans must ensure sufficient access to a range of providers that accept the non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full, including ECPs and providers specializing in mental health and substance use disorder services, to ensure services are accessible without unreasonable delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FFE States with Effective Provider Access Review Programs must ensure that QHPs meet access requirements in a manner consistent with section 1311(c)(1)(B).

rubrics_metrics.name: State provider access standards comparable to §§156.230(a)(1)(ii) and (iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: An FFE State must establish provider access standards set in State statute or regulation consistent with provider access standards at §§156.230(a)(1)(ii) and (iii) and relevant to non-network plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must show that their standards are applicable and relevant to non-network plan review.

rubrics_metrics.name: State reporting systems and documentation for provider access metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State must demonstrate that its provider access review process includes reporting systems for State-required provider access metrics related to non-network plans and documentation of methodologies associated with non-network plan review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must provide descriptions of data collection systems, templates, and methodologies sufficient to conduct examinations of non-network plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and timelines for regular provider access reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States must establish and maintain clear procedures and timeline requirements for regular provider access reviews related to non-network plans, including processes that ensure reviews occur prior to each plan year's QHP certification cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures reviews are timely and integrated with certification cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and addressing consumer-related provider access complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State must have a process for monitoring and addressing consumer-related provider access complaints for non-network plans to ensure sufficient access to providers consistent with section 1311(c)(1)(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaint monitoring is part of assessing whether access is adequate and responsive to consumer issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process to collect and review information demonstrating sufficient choice of accepting providers
rubrics_metrics.description: The FFE State must have a process to collect and review information capable of demonstrating whether non-network plans provide access to a sufficient choice of providers that accept the non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS seeks comments on whether States have processes in place to collect/analyze this information to demonstrate technical capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of qualitative factors per §156.236(b)(4)-(b)(9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of enumerating non-network plan submission requirements under §156.236(b)(4)-(b)(9) for FFE State review: assessing outreach strategies, publicizing benefit amounts, methodologies for determining benefit amounts, consumer-friendly balance billing information, availability of exceptions processes, and customer service resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are qualitative factors that may require different data collection methods than quantitative measures and HHS is seeking comment on aligning such reviews across FFEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE State Effective ECP Review Program criteria (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: An FFE State electing to conduct ECP certification reviews must demonstrate sufficient authority and technical capacity to be considered to have an Effective ECP Review Program under proposed §155.1051, including criteria specific to non-network plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State does not satisfy criteria, HHS would conduct ECP certification reviews under §156.235 (network) or proposed §156.236 (non-network).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network plan demonstration of reasonable and timely access to ECPs
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-network plan applying for QHP certification must demonstrate it provides reasonable and timely access to ECPs that accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full so services will be accessible without unreasonable delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In lieu of contract-based requirements for network plans, non-network plans must indicate benefit amounts as payment in full that were accepted by and/or offered to an ECP, per proposed §156.236(b)(1)-(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network plan ECP quantitative requirements (§156.236(b)(1)-(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans must meet minimum percentage requirements, the Indian health care provider requirement, and category per county requirements described in proposed §156.236(b)(1)-(b)(3) for ECP access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FFE States with Effective ECP Review Programs must demonstrate their ECP requirements are comparable to these proposed standards or explain how alternatives still ensure sufficient ECP access.

rubrics_metrics.name: State data collection and analytic capacity for ECP reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States must have adequate and accurate data on available ECPs, sufficient tools to collect issuer-submitted ECP data, and sound methodologies to quantitatively assess this data to ensure access to ECPs in accordance with section 1311(c)(1)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes structured analyses to measure adequacy of provider number and geographic distribution that accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full; Federal resources (e.g., Federal ECP List, MPMS) may be leveraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Federal ECP List or equivalent identification process
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the FFE State utilizes the Federal ECP List or has a process to identify qualified ECPs that may accept a non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full will be considered under §155.1051(e)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential to identify exact geographic location and distribution of ECPs that may accept benefit amounts to ensure statutory inclusion of ECPs 'where available.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of issuer information on status of offers to ECPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of whether the FFE State collects information from issuers regarding the status of offers of benefit amounts as payment in full to an ECP, as part of assessing compliance with minimum percentage, category per county, and Indian health care requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This data is an important metric for evaluating compliance with §156.236(b)(1)-(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring consumer-protective standards for low-income and medically underserved populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans and FFE State reviews must ensure minimum standards to protect low-income, medically underserved populations who rely on ECPs and may have lower insurance literacy and greater risk of high OOP costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special attention to expensive, specialized services furnished by ECPs (e.g., HIV/AIDS, cancer care, TB treatment, hemophilia) and to minimizing regressive OOP burdens for vulnerable populations.
